newsitem.title: FRANCE: Most traders say EU tender better-than-expected.
newsitem.headline: Most traders say EU tender better-than-expected.

text.p: Europe's decision on Thursday to raise the refund on soft wheat exports at this week's grain auction brought unexpectly good news to most traders, though some French traders said they had been expecting it.
The European Commission's grain committee awarded 211,350 tonnes of wheat at a rebate of 18.99 Ecus per tonne, four Ecus more than the refund granted the previous week.
In France exporters said the higher refund was in line with expectations but said the tonnages awarded of 200,000 tonnes were not enough to deal with the European Union's surplus.
"It is fairly normal, not a great surprise," one French exporter said.
But elsewhere in the EU, exporters were happy with the higher refund. "It's more than we were expecting. It's pretty aggressive," one exporter said
"I think they were quite generous, 200,000 tonnes is a good tonnage," one trader said.
Another trader said the higher refund showed the EU was not too concerned over a possible reaction from the United States because of the low tonnage awarded.
"As long as they keep the award in the 200,000 to 250,000 range they are not going to worry about a few Ecus," he said.
Exporters also said that a decline in world prices gave the European Union more leeway to step up export refunds.
"The EU is basically going along with the market," one exporter said.
But traders were quick to point out that if the EU award would help cover recent sales to Tunisia or Iraq, it was insufficient for business with Egypt.
"We need at least 20 Ecus for Egypt," one trader said.
Egypt bought 500,000 tonnes of French wheat at the start of the week.
The prices for deliveries in February, March and April, ranged from $140.50 to $143.90, per tonne Fob.
The latest EU wheat award values French wheat for late February at around $146 per tonne.
Traders were confident that the Commission would eventually relent although some said it may be reluctant to go above the psychological threshhold of 20 Ecus per tonne.
"It seems 20 Ecus is the magical number for wheat as 30 Ecus is for barley," one trader said.
On Tursday the EU grain panel sharply reduced barley exports to 26,000 tonnes from 256,800 tonnes last week, granting a refund of 29.79 Ecus per tonne.
In France exporters had bid for 220,000 tonnes exports at rebates ranging from 30.45 to 31.95 Ecus per tonne.
Grain industry sources linked the move to the EU's concern over firm domestic prices and suspicion of a possible squeeze by a few exporters.
